entries.title: Lao at a glance
body: Lao is the official language of Laos and a Tai–Kadai language, spoken by about 7 million people in Laos and by many more in northeast Thailand, where the Isan dialects are very close to it. Lao and Thai speakers can understand each other to a large degree.
Lao is tonal, with six tones in the Vientiane dialect. Words never change form: word order and helper words do the grammar.

examples.t: ຂ້ອຍ{ກຳລັງ}ຮຽນພາສາລາວ

entries.title: How Lao script works
body: Lao script is a sister of Thai script, simplified in the 20th century so that spelling follows pronunciation more closely. It has 27 consonant letters and vowel marks that sit before, after, above or below the consonant.

Words are written without spaces; a space marks the end of a phrase. Like Thai, consonants fall into high, middle and low classes, which together with the tone marks and the syllable type set each syllable's tone.

entries.title: Lao and Thai side by side
entries.body: Many letters are recognisably the same, and much basic vocabulary is shared, though some everyday words differ.

entries.title: The baci ceremony
entries.body: A baci (ບາສີ) marks weddings, births, departures and the New Year. Guests tie white cotton strings around each other's wrists while wishing health and luck, calling back the 32 souls (ຂວັນ) believed to keep a person whole. The strings are left on for at least three days.
